The core insight is that conciseness is not merely stylistic but a form of entropy minimization in design space. The operator \min H(X) subject to \mathcal{M}(X) = Y formalizes how reducing design complexity while preserving intelligence payload achieves optimal communication. Data-as-intelligence extends this by asserting that layout and aesthetics are merely transformations of raw data, not independent sources of meaning. Subtractive design operationalizes this by defining a set of redundant elements \Delta X that can be removed without loss of \mathcal{M}(X) = Y. These primitives form a dual framework: one for encoding information efficiently (GSI), another for navigating state spaces effectively (GSE). Failure modes include over-design (entropy inflation) and under-design (information loss).
